findings.title: The inward image at the perceptual threshold
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the deity is also the orientation of the inward human image at a perceptual interface where subtle signals can reshape later action.
findings.mechanism: The focus people form carries the exact qualified pupil-image branch; hidden low sound in 114:4 and the action-source image in 114:5 supply independent context. Their contact shifts the people in the title from externally visible bodies toward a vulnerable inner representation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see a small image of the self inside perception and understand how a barely heard signal could alter what that self later does.
findings.containment: This is an optical analogy, not a lexical translation of الناس as pupil. The ordinary people meaning, the anatomical/contextual alternatives, and the exploratory status remain visible.

epistemic.reason: The outlier has exact focus and contextual coordinates and an explicit containment boundary, but it is an exploratory optical analogy from a legacy_unbound trace.

findings.title: Agency hidden in the crowd
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus concerns allegiance within a crowd whose density can hide agency and circulate influence without a visible author.
findings.mechanism: The focus worship and human-collective branches contact the closing coordination of hidden beings and humans, with an attributed dark-mass/crowd facet under ج ن ن. The contact folds visible peoplehood into a social-opacity analogy while preserving the focus relation to worship.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a second kind of concealment: pressure may be hard to attribute because it moves through a dense visible collective.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading still distinguishes الجنة and الناس; the focus word is not translated as crowd-concealment and the two nouns are not identified. This remains an exploratory social analogy.

epistemic.reason: The exact closing coordination and focus return are supplied, while the crowd-opacity arrow is explicitly exploratory and the context branch is unresolved in the registry.

findings.title: A course that can veer
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus is an orienting course of human allegiance, while whispering appears as a concealed lateral deviation that can occur during apparent forward motion.
findings.mechanism: The focus worship and person-facing branches contact an attributed governed road/valley image in 114:2 and a horse's veering image in 114:4. The contact changes the focus from a destination named apart from movement into an orientation whose course can be deflected.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see deviation as a sideways alteration of direction rather than only a final state of being lost, while the worship title remains the orienting relation.
findings.containment: The focus remains a deity-title and the context remains a protector/threat sequence. This is a spatial analogy from an exploratory legacy_unbound trace, not a lexical meaning of any focus word; the ordinary title and harm readings remain live.

epistemic.reason: The route and veering coordinates are exact and the trace states a concrete before/after change, but the spatial arrow is explicitly exploratory with unresolved contextual branches.

findings.title: The external worship act
findings.claim: The separately added 1:5 makes the focus title newly audible as the object of an explicit first-person plural act of worship.
findings.mechanism: The focus worship branch is carried by إِلَٰهِ; the external context occurrence نَعْبُدُ at 1:5:2 independently names worship. Their contact turns the title from a nominal relation alone into the named direction of a communal act, adding a specific overlay beyond the native pericope findings.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the title to an enacted collective orientation rather than only to the existence of a deity over the people.
findings.containment: This is an external macro overlay only. It does not identify the pronoun we with the noun الناس, import the whole Fatiha argument, or replace the native title/protection readings. The other added ayat were not retained because they supplied no separate local contact with changed understanding.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is lexicon-resolved and the external 1:5 surface/root occurrence is exact, but the selected external unit is a lean context projection without target morphology or an HFT support record.

branch_activations.boundary: The external pronoun is not equated with الناس, and the overlay does not import a whole-surah Fatiha thesis.
